newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to open telcoms market in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Israel to open telcoms market in 1998.

text.p: Israel's entire telecommunications market will be open to competition by the end of 1998, Communications Minister Limor Livnat said at a news conference on Tuesday.

"Our internal telecom market will open up to competition in a wide range of areas," Livnat said, adding this would be the last segment of opening the market. "With completion of this, every Israeli...can obtain better service, choose from a wider range of offers and pay a cheaper price."
She said the government would introduce competition in telecoms infrastructure, and in inter-urban and local calling -- areas today controlled exclusively by state-owned Bezeq Israel Telecom.

The three are the last remaining segments of the Israeli telecoms market controlled by Bezeq, after the opening of the cellular telephony, international calling and other smaller telecoms services over the last five years.

Livnat said the criteria for allowing new competitors into the three new areas would be determined by the end of 1997 after technical and economic aspects of the new competition had been fully examined.

She said initially only a limited number of operators would be licensed to operate in the new areas. Additional competitors might be then allowed, depending on the success of the first phase of limited competition.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor termed the changes "one of the most important structural changes in the economy".

The recommendations, based on a joint Communications-Finance Ministry committee's report, will be given to the cabinet Friday, Livnat said. She vowed that Bezeq would be compensated for its lost monopolies by being allowed to enter segments now barred to it.
